questions.q: Why did Agassi resent tennis as a child?
a: His father pushed him relentlessly from a young age
He was injured and could not play for years
His coaches ignored his early talent
He preferred team sports to individual ones
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Agassi hitting thousands of balls daily while his father yelled instructions.

questions.q: What did Agassi's father hope his son would win?
a: An Olympic medal
A Wimbledon trophy
A college scholarship
A national junior title
questions.why: Lesson 1 says his father's own Olympic failure made him determined that his son would win a medal.

questions.q: What did Ivan Lendl say about young Agassi?
a: That he was a haircut and forehand
That he would break every record
That he lacked any real talent
That he was the next Bjorn Borg
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes Ivan Lendl dismissing the young Agassi as a haircut and forehand.

questions.q: What helped Agassi find purpose after hitting rock bottom?
a: Founding a school for at-risk children
Winning his first Grand Slam title
Buying a house in Las Vegas
Retiring from professional tennis
questions.why: Lesson 3 says building a school for at-risk children helped free him from self-loathing.

questions.q: What does Agassi say about transformation at the end of his career?
a: You are never a finished product and always in progress
Success ends once you retire from competition
Fame is the only real reward for an athlete
He had finally become a finished champion
questions.why: Lesson 3 reports Agassi saying you can never be a finished product and everyone is in progress.
